## Design

### 2026-10-10 – Oct 9 2026

**4.5h**

Oct 9 2026
I wanted to make a cool hardware project but I didn't have any experience so I decided to go with the guided project AKA the Starbie. I created the schematic for the hardware which wasn't too difficult. The only hard part was trying not to get overwhelmed by the sheer amount of components in the placer. But by the end of hour 1, with help from the guide and Youtube. I was able to create the schematic for the Starbie

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 215821](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/FrwjC1X5XOInayrnpPDTeLMtHsB5eUED/632a045802eae4b15cedfb1891592b901a53d08f6620a61f4e2139eba919e089.png)

After that, I had to create the copper connections between everything so that it actually worked. This step took me 3 hours (which I am not proud of) mostly because I refused to turning the components because I thought something might mess up if I did rotate some. But after that problem was resolved, everything became pretty straight forward and I was able to create the PCB design for the Starbie (the blue lines are the connections.

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 215443](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/FrwjC1X5XOInayrnpPDTeLMtHsB5eUED/99e5ba7c4d3cc103562d74cae09f4a8839b5bbc76b5f580400f2430d069186ef.png)

After I created that, I realized that I hadn't even made a repo for the project yet. So I set up the github repo for the Starbie which took like 5 mins because mostly everything was made and all I had to do was add it in.

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 220348](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/FrwjC1X5XOInayrnpPDTeLMtHsB5eUED/642b2d5f750524d8ad262b5f270854253492914ae036eaa612fde273e25571aa.png)

While the guide was good, there were a good amount of times where I had to rely on the internet or Youtube to find how to do a step properly. While I didn't use too many videos, some actually helped me quite a bit. Like this one,

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 220733](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/FrwjC1X5XOInayrnpPDTeLMtHsB5eUED/33101b32731badfab56ac07dc30a58a380d52081e9371065ec52c325d44c73c8.png)

Now I am on the customization step of the starbie, and I cant wait to continue working on it!

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 171413](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/FrwjC1X5XOInayrnpPDTeLMtHsB5eUED/469e25708b198a003d9f169d676f661172775a16b1d4840479e0c250e8768224.png)

### 2026-10-10 – Oct 10 2026

**5.5h**

Oct 10 2026

Today I have finished the Starbie project! At least, most of it (I cant debug the code right now since I dont have an arduino). Firstly, I customized it a bit by adding a character onto the PCB. I was going to customize it some more but I ran out of ideas. So for now, it has only one character/design on it.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 190241](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/FrwjC1X5XOInayrnpPDTeLMtHsB5eUED/35d9ae416b63991efac7c5d21d27e2fc5d287464c4e1d7145adb685a08ebfa32.png)

After that, I had to download the Arduino IDE so I could code the PCB ( The code came from the guide). It didn't take that long to actually get the code, and I actually ran into no problems with the code setup.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 193443](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/FrwjC1X5XOInayrnpPDTeLMtHsB5eUED/154385a2f48722089a2509ddbf77b3c6c7fdf89322d11e998cc4dd6015f86bef.png)

I did want to change the character inside the starbie, so I did! I added the same character that is on the PCB as the character. The picture looks something like this

![simple chopper](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/FrwjC1X5XOInayrnpPDTeLMtHsB5eUED/ad08e8da167e6a9b6f7c8d3c8ef3dd1cf751876b3ae75a7cfdb3e90c70b6bd8f.png)

But I realized that it was too colorful and too big to fit into the starbie, so I had to send the image through various different websites so it would become black and white as well as 32x32 px. So it went from looking like the character above, to looking like it looks like now.

![simple_chopper-removebg-preview-modified-32x32](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/FrwjC1X5XOInayrnpPDTeLMtHsB5eUED/ac6d7650d3013729d2b4dbd93ee5dfc1bdeac2f81df9b78f66a399240c6e31fd.png)

After that, I had to get the byte list for the character so he could be print out well. So I used the website from the guide and got it designed but it didnt look good at all. So I changed how many bits per pixel there were. Instead of 1 bit per pixel horizontally, I made it 2 bits per pixel horizontally and that made the character actually look like a character. This is how it looked with 1 bit per pixel horizontally.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 214230](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/FrwjC1X5XOInayrnpPDTeLMtHsB5eUED/124c298e073ef9048ce15bb0bafcbe45d028f9fcb04aa1a440cf5653e478c2ad.png)

And with 2 bit per pixel horizontally it looked like this.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 214351](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/FrwjC1X5XOInayrnpPDTeLMtHsB5eUED/714217c980e76c5b84c77f4d18039d0ab1eb227f1b4cba099ad4745abfc061ac.png)

As you can see, it looks a lot better, but I don't know if this will work or if it'll be too detailed for the PCB's screen to actually handle. If it is, then I will have to use the less detailed one. Otherwise, I have finished the starbie project!
